page: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 3.0 GHz, with a single thread per core and no hyperthreading overhead. Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of RAM allocated per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic extensions. The server does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached Premium Storage volumes for persistent disk operations.

Performance benchmarks reflect the architectural profile of the Ampere Neoverse-N1 design. In multi-core compute scenarios, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 7249.86 and a single-core score of 1822.69, both aligning with median benchmark expectations. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 50.14 GB/sec for reads and 29.77 GB/sec for writes on large blocks, matching mid-tier averages, while PassMark database operations posted a balanced result of 2932.98. Conversely, synthetic compute suites show lower relative output, with Geekbench single-core at 1122.0 and multi-core at 3707.0. Tasks requiring specialized vector extensions or heavy floating-point calculation face constraints due to the lack of AVX instruction sets.

By leveraging power-efficient ARM architecture, the E4ps_v5 provides economical access to substantial memory allocations without the resource overhead of high-frequency x86 compute tiers. This hardware profile delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for environments where RAM capacity dictates deployment sizing rather than raw per-thread compute throughput. The server is suited for memory-bound services such as in-memory caching nodes, relational databases with moderate query complexity, static web serving tiers, and containerized microservices compiled for arm64 runtimes.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture, powered by a 4-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance allocates 32 GB of memory across 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, delivering a high memory-to-CPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It includes no bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on external Premium Storage for disk operations. Benchmark data indicates average execution in multi-core stress testing and database operations, alongside average uncached memory read and write bandwidth. However, Geekbench metrics, integer tests, and LLM inference fall into lower percentile tiers. The instance delivers cost efficiency through power-efficient ARM core utilization and high memory allocation per vCPU. Microsoft Azure E4ps_v5 is suitable for memory-intensive workloads including mid-sized relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, static web application serving, and ARM-native background processing tasks.
